_meta.indication: Treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), to include clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel group, active comparator-controlled trial versus teriflunomide 14 mg orally, 96 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with relapsing forms of MS who had experienced at least one relapse in the previous year, two relapses in the previous two years, or a T1 Gd-enhancing lesion in the previous year, with baseline EDSS 0 to 5.5.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: annualized relapse rate (ARR) over the treatment period.
pivotal_trials.n: 274 randomized to BRIUMVI and 275 to teriflunomide.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel group, active comparator-controlled trial of identical design to Study 1, versus teriflunomide, 96 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with relapsing forms of MS, same enrollment criteria as Study 1 (relapse history or T1 Gd-enhancing lesion; baseline EDSS 0 to 5.5).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: annualized relapse rate (ARR) over the treatment period.
pivotal_trials.n: 272 randomized to BRIUMVI and 273 to teriflunomide.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) were infusion reactions and upper respiratory tract infections. Infusion reactions occurred in 48% (vs 12% teriflunomide) and upper respiratory tract infections in 45% (vs 41%). Serious infections were higher with BRIUMVI (5% vs 3%), and there were 3 infection-related deaths, all in BRIUMVI-treated patients (post-measles encephalitis, pneumonia, and post-operative salpingitis).
target_moa: A glycoengineered chimeric anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody that binds CD20 on pre-B and mature B lymphocytes, causing B-cell depletion via antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-dependent cytotoxicity.
modality: mAb (glycoengineered chimeric murine/human anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody)

rems.type: DRM and DN2 agreed that a REMS is not necessary to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of ublituximab.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class and did not raise unexpected safety or efficacy issues.

summary.text: Standard BLA (351(a)) received September 28, 2021 with a PDUFA goal date of December 28, 2022 (extended three months from 09/28/2022 by major amendments); approved December 28, 2022 as a full (traditional) approval based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials, without accelerated approval, priority review, breakthrough, or orphan designations, and without referral to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Please refer to your biologics license application (BLA) dated and received September 28, 2021, and your amendments, submitted under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act for Briumvi (ublituximab-xiiy) injection for intravenous use.

The applicant presents the results from two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 clinical trials, Studies TG1101-RMS301 and TG1101-RMS302 (Studies RMS301 and RMS302 hereafter) as the basis of an application to support a claim of safety and efficacy for ublituximab-xiiy in the treatment of relapsing forms of MS.

Your application for Briumvi (ublituximab-xiiy) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class, the safety profile is similar to that of other biologics approved for this indication, the clinical trial designs are acceptable, and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a biologic in this class.

requirement.text: 4337-4: A pregnancy outcomes study using a different study design to assess pregnancy complications, major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, preterm births, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to Briumvi during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 4337-6: A safety trial to monitor serum immunoglobulin G and M levels in RMS patients during treatment with Briumvi to establish the nadir during chronic treatment and time to restoration after discontinuation, capturing infection rates and B-cell counts.
